title: Positive Emotions via Mental Imagery
summary: When people are depressed they often no longer enjoy or look forward to activities or events. This aspect of depression, called "anhedonia", is often not improved by standard treatments. Results from previous research suggest that one promising method to improve anhedonia may be a simple computerized training program, in which participants repeatedy practice imagining positive scenes or events. This study aims to develop one form of this training, "Picture-Word Training", in which photos with positive captions are used as the basis for imagining the positive scenes. In this study the training will be tailored to each individual particants as the photos used in the training will be photos from the participants' daily lives, which they provide themselves. The study will be conducted as a "single case series" to allow development and refinement of the training over the course of the study. Adult participants experiencing at least moderate levels of anhedonia and at least mild levels of depression will first spend either one or two weeks providing ratings of anhedonia, mood, thoughts, and activity twice per day via their smartphone. They will then spend one week completing one session of the picture-word training on their own laptop each day, in addition to the smartphone ratings. Participants will then complete online follow-up questionnaires two and four weeks after the end of the training.  The study will provide preliminary indications of whether the training could be effective or not and provide a starting point for future randomized controlled trials of the training.
conditions: Adults aged 18-40 experiencing at least moderate levels of anhedonia and at least mild levels of depression symptoms

interventions.name: One week of daily "picture-word" computerized positive imagery training

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Fluent written and spoken German
•	Own a smartphone that is compatible with the SEMA3 ecological momentary assessment software (iOS 8 or later, Android 6.0 or later, not Huawei or Oppo) 
•	Own a laptop that is compatible with the study (able to run Java-based programs)
•	Motivated and able to attend all study appointments and complete all study procedures
•	Scoring ≥ 2 on item 1 (“Little interest or pleasure in doing things”) of the PHQ-9 (Kroenke et al., 2001), indicating at least moderate levels of anhedonia, and scoring ≥ 5 in total on the PHQ-9, indicating at least mild levels of depression symptoms.
Exclusion criteria:
•	Currently receiving psychological or pharmacological treatment for a psychological disorder or stress.
•	Currently in a crisis state requiring an acute treatment (e.g., suicidality)
